note: The content_hash vectors are FROZEN, and they do not come from the C# in src/. They were produced by a reference implementation of Translation::computeHash — the website's — and that implementation was itself checked against reality first: run over a real 690-line published translation sitting on disk, it reproduced the file_hash the server had issued for that file. So these are not 'what our code does', they are what the server does. A hash that only agrees with itself would pass every check and make every translation in existence look permanently out of sync.

in.lines: object keyed by the game's text, each a line in the file's form

content_hash.out: 64 lowercase hex, the sha-256 of the canonical document

is_metadata_key.out: bool: a key the tools write about a file, not a line of it

in.local_content: hash of what is on disk
in.server_content: file_hash the server reports, or null when unknown
in.last_synced: the server hash this file was last in step with, or null when never synced

name.out: the two or three words a player reads

explain.out: what follows from it, in one sentence

cases.why: an empty translation still hashes — the uuid is content too
the tag is part of the content, not a decoration

keys sort by byte, not by culture — ORDINAL puts 'A' before '_uuid' before 'a'; a culture-aware sort puts 'a' first and produces a different document on one machine and not another — and the uuid sorts among them
accents stay as themselves — literal, not escaped: both are valid JSON, only one is the right bytes (JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE, and the mod agrees)
and so does anything else — the games that most need translating are these ones
a solidus is not escaped — PHP escapes it unless told not to; we tell it not to
quotes are escaped, in keys as well as in values
and so are backslashes — a game full of \n literals would break otherwise
a tab uses its short form, not \u0009
a newline too — game text is full of them
and the rest go to lower-case \u00xx — four digits, whatever the character
metadata keys are excluded — a counter must not change a file's identity
the order they arrive in is irrelevant — two machines meet lines in different orders
the reference order of the case above
an absent tag stays absent: it is NOT filled in with the default — the file is hashed AS WRITTEN, and tidying anything produces a different hash for a file nobody edited
a null value stays null, not an empty string; they are different documents
a pre-tag entry stays a bare string — an old published file must still match
and the two forms coexist in one file, which is what an old file looks like
everything the tools write about a file starts with an underscore — the mod's convention, and the website's
a key the game showed is a line
only a LEADING underscore marks metadata
an empty key is nothing, not metadata
identical content is in sync, whatever the change counter says — asked FIRST: without it, a file edited back to what the server holds would be offered for upload forever
my changes on an unmoved server is an upload — nothing of theirs is at risk
their changes on an untouched file is a download — nothing of mine is at risk
both moved is a merge, and only the mod can settle it line by line
no ancestor plus local work is a conflict, not a download — that is a translation somebody built themselves and never published, and this case decides whether their work survives
no ancestor and nothing of mine is still a download — there is nothing to lose
nothing published means nothing to reconcile — not an upload nobody asked for
the four words every piece of software has used for thirty years: this read 'In step' until somebody pointed out that nobody outside a version-control habit says it
'Behind' said the same thing to nobody
'Ahead' said the same thing to nobody
'Diverged' is the version-control word; 'Conflict' is the one every program uses
